 BOZEMAN, Mont. — Montana State heads into its next home game with a ranked Weber State team coming to town after the Bobcats rolled past Eastern Washington in their first game after the bye week.
 The Wildcats will visit Bozeman for the fourth time in five years on Saturday in search of their first win in Bobcat Stadium since 2017. Montana State beat Weber State 66-14 last season, but head coach Brent Vigen said this version of the Wildcats looks different under first-year head coach Eric Kjar.
 "They're certainly playing with a ton of confidence that they had probably very little of when they came here last year. We're not spending a lot of time on last year's game, honestly, because it's, you know, entirely different coaching staff, but a lot of players are the same," said Vigen. "Last year, I felt like by the time they played us, they were a shell of what they had been at times, and there were injuries that factored in. I know they played, a number of quarterbacks. They've certainly, I think, settled in on a quarterback now," Vigen added.
 The quarterback Vigen referenced is true freshman Nate Dahle, who is expected to start under center for the Wildcats. He brings a running threat and leads Weber State in carries while also throwing for 1,591 yards and 16 touchdowns.
 He he's only completed 50 percent of his passes however and has thrown 10 interceptions. Vigen said making their offense one dimensional is the key for Montana State's defense.
 "When you get a young quarterback in obvious passing situations, what can we do to to make it hard and that's twofold for us. It's certainly the guys up front, but it's being able to to cover to give different looks on the back end. But the more pressure we can put on him, the better. That's ideally getting him to the ground a time or two and then maybe forcing some more ill advised throws at the same time," Vigen said.
 Montana State's offense is looking to build off its 49-point outing from the previous game against a Weber State defense that allows 34.1 points per game.
 Quarterback Justin Lamson said the Bobcats need to start fast and stay steady against a Weber State group he views as connected and competitive. 
 "Getting on them from the jump and just being consistent every single down and doing your job every single down. What I see out of Weber State so far from what I've watched, is, they're a very cohesive unit. They play really hard for their coaches and they're at the top of the conference. So, we need to bring our A-game just like we have to do it for everybody in this conference, Lamson said.
 Montana State is getting closer to full strength before their game on Saturday. Taco Dowler was not listed on the depth chart released at the start of the week, but Vigen said "there's a good chance" he would be available against the Wildcats after practicing this week.
 Burke Mastel and Colson Coon are also likely to play after missing the Eastern game, Vigen explained. He also said defensive lineman Dominic Solano is about a week away from returning.
 Montana State is set to host Weber State Saturday, October 24 at 1:00 p.m.
